# bugs #3744: The assemblers of the official Win64 builds crash on source lines that give a q error

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3744/
- Category: [Analyzed, not fixed](../../unresolved.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Keep open. Run the ticket's file with a current official Win64 build, and compare its toolchain with one that builds a working binary.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The crash does not occur with sdas8051 built from r17176 on Linux. The ticket's command,
`sdas8051 -l -o -s -a` on the three lines of the attached file, prints a `<q>` error for line 2 and
returns exit status 2. valgrind reports no error for this run. No Windows binary was run.

The reporter suggests in the last comment that the ticket can be closed. Bug #3763 shows that the
fault was still present in an official build after that comment.

## Known

- The assembler reports a `q` error for the ticket's input, and `xerr` in `sdas/asxxsrc/assubr.c`
  ends every `q` error with `longjmp(jump_env, -1)`. In a debugger run on r17176 the call chain is
  `main`, `asmbl`, `getdstr`, `xerr`, `longjmp`.
- This use of `longjmp` is valid C. `main` calls `setjmp` as an operand of the comparison that
  controls an `if` statement, which C11 7.13.1.1 paragraph 4 allows, and `main` is still active
  when `longjmp` is called, as C11 7.13.2.1 paragraph 2 requires. The two calls are the same in
  r14620, the revision of the 4.4.0 release.
- The reporter's screenshot shows `sdas8051.exe` on Windows 6.1.7601 with a fault in `ntdll.dll`
  and the exception code `c0000028`. Microsoft documents this code as `STATUS_BAD_STACK`.
- A commenter built Win64 binaries of sdas8051 and sdasz80 from the source with a MinGW-w64 cross
  compiler on Ubuntu 22.04, and these do not crash. The reporter found that the binary of the
  32-bit 4.4.0 installer does not crash.
- Bug #3763 reports the fault for another `q` error. Its third comment, of 2024-07-20, says that
  the binary of the official snapshot still crashes.

## Open

It is not known whether official Win64 builds made after July 2024 crash, and the cause in the
official build is not established. On 64-bit Windows `longjmp` unwinds the stack, so the exception
code is consistent with a failure in the `longjmp` call of the `q` error path. That is an inference
and was not tested. The next step is to compare the official cross toolchain with the commenter's
toolchain, which requires a Windows machine and access to the official build environment.

## Related

Bug #3763 is a duplicate of this ticket.
